I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor. My responsibilities today included keeping track of the bouquet, making sure Hannah had everything she needed, and remaining emotionally composed. Two out of three isn’t bad.

Being Hannah’s best friend means having someone who will celebrate your good news like she’s personally won an award—and show up on your bad days with snacks and absolutely no intention of leaving you alone with your thoughts.

A few years ago, we planned a picnic. Hannah had packed enough food for a small expedition. Naturally, the moment we were ready to leave, it started pouring.

I was prepared to cancel. Hannah moved the coffee table.

Ten minutes later, we were sitting on a blanket in her living room, eating sandwiches beside a houseplant she insisted provided “the outdoor atmosphere.” She also pointed out that this picnic had several advantages, including reliable plumbing.

I can’t remember what we’d originally planned to celebrate. I remember laughing until my stomach hurt.

That’s Hannah. She pays attention to what makes people happy, and then she does something about it. Sometimes that’s a thoughtful phone call. Sometimes it’s rearranging furniture to rescue a picnic.

Then Andrew came along.

When Hannah first told me about him, she was trying very hard to sound casual. Unfortunately, it’s difficult to sound casual when you’ve mentioned someone four times in a conversation that began with, “How was your weekend?”

But what made me happiest wasn’t just hearing about Andrew. It was seeing them together.

Andrew, you listen to Hannah with real interest—even when a story requires several introductions and a brief explanation of who knows whom. You make her laugh that completely unguarded laugh I know so well. And I love seeing how much fun she has with you.

Hannah, I’ve had the privilege of being beside you through so many versions of life. Seeing you here today, so happy and so completely yourself, means more to me than I can fit into a speech. Especially one I promised to keep reasonably short.

You and Andrew have something wonderful: affection, friendship, and the ability to enjoy each other’s company when there’s no occasion to dress up for.

My wish for you is that you keep making time for that. Keep telling each other the small, ridiculous details of your days. Keep finding reasons to celebrate. And if the picnic gets rained out, I hope you’ll always be happy to move the coffee table together.

Everyone, please raise a glass.

To Hannah and Andrew: a home full of laughter, a lifetime of friendship, and many excellent reasons to open the good snacks.

Cheers!"}
